title: Admin - Comment Moderation - Filter by Status - Functional Test Plan
overview: Functional testing of the Admin Comment Moderation - Filter by Status feature on the Y4J platform. This feature provides a status filter with options (All Status, Pending, Approved, Rejected) that dynamically updates the moderation list. 'Needs Review' and 'Vendor Flagged' items are grouped under 'Pending'. The filter works in combination with search. Covers filter options, dynamic updates, grouping logic, filter+search integration, and empty state.

testCases.title: Status filter is visible with correct options
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Comment Moderation page is loaded.
steps: Click/open the filter to see available options
expectedResults: A status filter control is visible on the page
The filter shows four options: 'All Status', 'Pending', 'Approved', 'Rejected'
All options are selectable
The default selection is 'All Status'
testCases.postconditions: Status filter is confirmed visible with correct options

testCases.title: Selecting 'All Status' shows all moderation items
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Items with various statuses exist.
expectedResults: All moderation items are displayed regardless of status
Items with Pending, Approved, and Rejected statuses are all visible
The list is unfiltered
The count reflects the total number of items

testCases.title: Selecting 'Pending' shows only pending items
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Items with 'Needs Review' or 'Vendor Flagged' status exist.
expectedResults: Only items with pending-related statuses are displayed
Items with 'Needs Review' status are shown (grouped under Pending)
Items with 'Vendor Flagged' status are shown (grouped under Pending)
Items with 'Approved' or 'Rejected' status are NOT shown
The list updates dynamically without page reload

testCases.title: Selecting 'Approved' shows only approved items
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Items with 'Approved' status exist.
expectedResults: Only items with 'Approved' status are displayed
No 'Pending', 'Needs Review', 'Vendor Flagged', or 'Rejected' items are shown
Each visible card shows 'Approved' status badge
The list updates dynamically

testCases.title: Selecting 'Rejected' shows only rejected items
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Items with 'Rejected' status exist.
expectedResults: Only items with 'Rejected' status are displayed
No 'Pending', 'Approved', or other status items are shown
Each visible card shows 'Rejected' status badge
The list updates dynamically

testCases.title: Selecting a filter updates the list immediately
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Moderation items exist.
expectedResults: The list updates immediately after selecting the filter
No page reload occurs
The transition is smooth (no flickering or delay)
The selected filter is visually indicated
testCases.postconditions: List updates immediately on filter change

testCases.title: Needs Review items are grouped under Pending filter
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Items with 'Needs Review' status exist.
steps: Look for items with 'Needs Review' status badge
expectedResults: Items with 'Needs Review' status are visible when 'Pending' filter is selected
These items are correctly grouped under the Pending category
They are NOT shown when 'Approved' or 'Rejected' filter is selected
testCases.postconditions: Needs Review is confirmed grouped under Pending

testCases.title: Vendor Flagged items are grouped under Pending filter
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Items with 'Vendor Flagged' status exist.
steps: Look for items with 'Vendor Flagged' status badge
expectedResults: Items with 'Vendor Flagged' status are visible when 'Pending' filter is selected
These items are correctly grouped under the Pending category
They are NOT shown when 'Approved' or 'Rejected' filter is selected
testCases.postconditions: Vendor Flagged is confirmed grouped under Pending

testCases.title: Filter works along with search
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Items with various statuses and searchable content exist.
steps: Type a search query in the search field
expectedResults: Results are filtered by BOTH the status filter AND the search query
Only items matching both criteria are shown
The search does not clear the status filter
The status filter does not clear the search
Combined filtering works correctly

testCases.title: Empty results for selected filter shows 'No results found'
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A filter combination that yields no results exists.
steps: Select a status filter that has no matching items
OR apply a filter + search combination that yields no results
expectedResults: No moderation cards are displayed
A 'No results found' message (or similar empty state) is shown
The message is clearly visible
The filter selection remains active
The user can change the filter to see results again
testCases.postconditions: Empty state is displayed for no-match filter

testCases.title: Switching between filters updates results correctly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Items with various statuses exist.
steps: Switch to 'Approved' filter — note the results
Switch to 'Rejected' filter — note the results
expectedResults: Each filter switch updates the list immediately
Results are different for each filter (unless all items have the same status)
Switching back to 'All Status' restores the full list
No stale data from previous filter remains

testCases.title: Filter selection persists after page refresh
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A filter is selected.
expectedResults: After refresh, the filter resets to 'All Status' (default behavior)
OR the filter persists (if state is maintained)
Either behavior is acceptable as long as it's consistent
The list matches the displayed filter state
testCases.postconditions: Filter state is consistent after refresh

testCases.title: Filter is visually highlighted when active
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin.
expectedResults: The selected filter option is visually highlighted or indicated
The admin can clearly see which filter is currently active
The selected state is distinguishable from unselected options
